x: Lothal in Gujarat was the Harappan port-town with a brick dockyard used for maritime trade. Kalibangan is an inland Harappan site, and Korkai and Puhar are Sangam ports.

x: Arikamedu near Puducherry has yielded Roman amphorae, Arretine ware and other Roman objects, marking it as an Indo-Roman trading station of the Sangam period.

I, II, III and IV are correct: pearls, corals, silk and pepper all appear among the goods traded at Motupalli.

x: Lothal was a Harappan dock, Korkai a Pandya port of Roman trade, Puhar the early Chola port-capital, and Tamralipti the port for North Indian trade with South-East Asia and China, giving a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv.

x: All four were major western-coast ports of the Sangam age: Naura, Tondi, Mushiri (Muziris) and Nelisanda, mainly in the Chera country.
t: Recall the west-coast ports of the Sangam age.

x: I, II and III are correct: Naura was a Sangam-age port on the western coast and took part in maritime trade.
I, II and III are correct: Tondi was a Sangam-age port on the western Chera coast and took part in maritime trade.
Both are true: Mushiri, the Muziris of Greek and Roman writers, was a Sangam-age port on the western coast in the Chera region, near present Kodungallur.
Both are true: Muziris was a major western-coast port and a leading centre of maritime trade with the Roman world.
Both are true: Nelisanda was a Sangam-age port on the western coast, active in maritime trade and counted among the major ports there.
I, II, III and IV are correct: Puhar, also called Poompuhar and Kaveri Poompattinam, was a Chola port in Tamil Nadu at the mouth of the Kaveri, active in sea trade.

x: Vasco da Gama arrived in 1498, returned in 1502 and made his last visit in 1524, giving B, C, A.

t: Check the year in each statement.
